title: African Union: Continental Education Strategy for Africa 2026–2035
note: The 2026–2035 strategy updates the 2016–2025 strategy and covers education for children, youth and adults in Africa.
limits: Overview only; not a specific admissions rule, individual career assessment or proof of job demand.
review_method: Primary publisher page inspected; short paraphrase only

title: World Bank: Africa’s Pulse, October 2025
section: Policy Recommendations: human capital and jobs-rich sectors
note: The October 2025 analysis recommends skills development connected to industry needs. It identifies agribusiness, tourism, health care, construction, digital services and manufacturing as sectors with job-creation potential.
limits: Regional potential is not a forecast of vacancies or salaries in a particular country. Confirm local labour-market data.
review_method: Primary publisher page inspected; short paraphrase only

title: European Commission: About ESCO
note: ESCO connects occupations with skills and knowledge through a multilingual classification. Its dataset is available for consultation and download.
limits: Use as a vocabulary aid, not proof of African demand, local licensing or equivalent qualifications. Specific occupation records have not been imported.
review_method: Primary publisher page inspected; short paraphrase only

title: DAAD: Doctoral Programmes in Germany
note: Selection considers qualifications, research quality and feasibility, and applicant potential. The programme distinguishes a motivation letter from a self-authored research proposal and requires evidence of supervision or programme contact as appropriate.
scope: This DAAD doctoral funding programme in Germany
limits: Not a universal scholarship rule. Check country eligibility, current call, deadlines and portal status. A letter alone is not a complete application.
review_method: Primary publisher page inspected; short paraphrase only

title: UCAS: Personal statement for 2026 entry onwards
note: The statement uses three answers covering motivation for the subject, preparation through study, and preparation outside education. Each answer requires at least 350 characters; all answers share a 4,000-character allowance including spaces.
limits: The statement is shared across choices. Verify the current portal rules and use the applicant’s own reflections.
review_method: Primary publisher page inspected; short paraphrase only

title: Cambridge: PhD in Public Health and Primary Care
section: Things You’ll Need; How to Find a Supervisor
note: This course requires a statement of interest limited to 2,500 characters and a separate proposed-supervisors field. Applicants should investigate research fit and contact potential supervisors. The Gates Cambridge route also asks PhD applicants for a research proposal.
limits: Do not apply its limits to other Cambridge programmes. Do not invent a supervisor or imply acceptance. Confirm current application requirements.
review_method: Primary publisher page inspected; short paraphrase only

title: UNICEF: Global Framework on Transferable Skills (2019)
note: The framework supports integrating transferable skills into formal, non-formal and community learning throughout life. It addresses policymakers, educators and programme teams.
limits: Not a university admissions rubric or evidence that an applicant possesses a skill.
review_method: Primary publisher page inspected; short paraphrase only

title: UNESCO: Strategy for TVET 2022–2029
note: TVET supports skills for employment, entrepreneurship and fulfilling work, including digital and green transitions. The strategy covers 2022–2029.
limits: Not proof that a particular course is accredited, free, available or accepted by an employer.
review_method: Primary publisher page inspected; short paraphrase only

title: CareerOneStop: Find career ideas
note: Career exploration can combine reflection on interests, skills and work values with research into occupations, followed by narrowing the options.
scope: Career exploration method from a US Department of Labor-sponsored resource
limits: US wages, training systems and local service listings do not transfer automatically to African countries.
review_method: Primary publisher page inspected; short paraphrase only

title: African Continental Qualifications Framework
note: ACQF connects national and regional qualifications work across Africa and supports transparency, lifelong learning and learner/worker mobility. Its portal includes national qualifications authorities and recognition-of-prior-learning resources.
limits: A framework reference is not automatic equivalence or professional registration. Confirm recognition with the destination institution and national qualifications authority.
review_method: Primary programme overview inspected; short paraphrase only
